assembly_instructions: Abstract microarchitecture block diagram, not a physical machine — there is no real-world scale, so the scene is laid out ~17.5 m wide purely for legibility. Build the black PCB backplane first (centered at origin, bottom edge on the grid). Mount every functional block as a box standing proud of the front face (+Z). Pipeline flows left-to-right along +X: front end (L1 I-cache with its I-cache MSHR and instruction TLB, a global history register feeding the TAGE predictor, BTB, return address stack, fetch target queue, fetch unit, fetch buffer) → decode → register rename (map table, free list, busy table) with a per-branch rename checkpoint → dispatch → issue queues → physical register files → reorder buffer with commit/retire logic → execution units (two integer ALUs, branch unit, integer mul/div, two FP pipelines) wrapped by an operand bypass/forwarding network → load-store unit with its data TLB → load queue, store queue → L1 D-cache with its D-cache MSHR; a page table walker in the lower right refills both TLBs. The speculative out-of-order structures — rename map table, free list, busy table, branch snapshot, the three issue queues, the tall ROB bank, the TLBs, GHR, RAS, FTQ and commit logic — are rendered in white composite so they read prominently against the black board. Copper buses are laid flat on the backplane surface tracing the pipeline, branch-redirect, writeback and memory paths.

info.japanese_name: BOOM（バークレー・アウトオブオーダー・マシン）
info.summary: BOOM is an open-source superscalar, out-of-order RISC-V core generator developed at UC Berkeley. It implements the full RV64GC ISA and is widely used in academic and industrial microarchitecture research.
info.description: BOOM is a synthesizable, parameterized out-of-order processor written in the Chisel hardware construction language, which elaborates to Verilog. Its datapath spans roughly ten pipeline stages: a decoupled front end with a TAGE-L branch predictor, branch target buffer and return address stack feeds a fetch target queue and fetch buffer; instructions are then decoded, register-renamed against a map table with an explicit free list and busy table, dispatched into separate integer, memory and floating-point issue queues, and executed out of order against unified physical register files. A reorder buffer (ROB) tracks in-flight instructions and enforces precise, in-order commit and speculation recovery.
info.description_extra: The current generation, BOOMv3 — also called SonicBOOM (2020) — added a load/store unit with decoupled load and store queues, an improved TAGE predictor, and short-forwards branch optimization, reaching competitive IPC for an academic core. BOOM ships as part of the Chipyard SoC framework and reuses the Rocket Chip non-blocking caches, TLBs, page table walker and TileLink interconnect.
info.operator: UC Berkeley Architecture Research (BAR) group and the RISC-V community
info.contractor: University of California, Berkeley — EECS / SLICE Lab

facts.label: Branch predictor
facts.value: TAGE-L + BTB + RAS, global history register

facts.label: Address translation
facts.value: Sv39/Sv48 ITLB + DTLB, shared page table walker

sources.title: SonicBOOM: The 3rd Generation Berkeley Out-of-Order Machine (CARRV 2020)

parts.name: Block-diagram backplane (PCB)
parts.role: Root structural board that all functional blocks and copper buses are mounted on.

parts.name: L1 Instruction Cache
parts.role: Supplies instruction bytes to the fetch unit each cycle.

parts.name: I-Cache Miss-Status Holding Registers
parts.role: Tracks outstanding instruction-cache misses so the front end stays non-blocking while a refill is in flight.

parts.name: Instruction TLB
parts.role: Translates instruction virtual addresses to physical addresses for every fetch; a miss traps to the page table walker.

parts.name: Global History Register
parts.role: Shift register of recent branch outcomes that indexes the TAGE-L tagged tables and is corrected on every branch resolution.

parts.name: TAGE-L Branch Predictor
parts.role: Speculatively predicts branch directions from tagged-geometric history so the front end can run ahead of resolution.

parts.name: Branch Target Buffer (BTB)
parts.role: Predicts branch target addresses to steer the next fetch before the branch is decoded.

parts.name: Return Address Stack (RAS)
parts.role: Stack of recent call sites that predicts return-instruction targets for the front end.

parts.name: Fetch Target Queue (FTQ)
parts.role: Buffers predicted fetch addresses, decoupling the branch predictor from instruction fetch and holding branch metadata until resolution.

parts.name: Instruction Fetch Unit
parts.role: Fetches a packet of instructions per cycle using the predicted PC stream from the FTQ.

parts.name: Fetch Buffer
parts.role: Decouples the front end from the back end, queuing fetched instructions for decode.

parts.name: Decode Stage
parts.role: Expands fetched bytes into micro-ops and reads architectural register specifiers.

parts.name: Rename Map Table
parts.role: Maps architectural registers to physical registers, removing false dependencies for out-of-order execution.

parts.name: Branch Snapshot / Rename Checkpoint
parts.role: Captures a checkpoint of the rename map table and front-end state for each in-flight branch, restored verbatim on a mispredict.

parts.name: Free List
parts.role: Tracks unallocated physical registers and hands one to each renamed destination.

parts.name: Busy Table
parts.role: Records whether each physical register's value is ready, feeding wakeup logic in the issue queues.

parts.name: Dispatch Stage
parts.role: Steers renamed micro-ops into the appropriate issue queue and allocates ROB entries.

parts.name: Integer Issue Queue
parts.role: Holds integer micro-ops and issues them out of order once their operands wake up.

parts.name: Memory Issue Queue
parts.role: Issues load and store address micro-ops out of order to the load-store unit.

parts.name: Floating-Point Issue Queue
parts.role: Issues floating-point micro-ops out of order to the FP pipelines.

parts.name: Integer Physical Register File
parts.role: Large unified store of integer physical registers read by execution units and written by writeback.

parts.name: Floating-Point Physical Register File
parts.role: Holds floating-point physical registers feeding and capturing results from the FP pipelines.

parts.name: Reorder Buffer (ROB)
parts.role: Tall bank tracking every in-flight instruction in program order to enforce precise commit and speculation recovery.

parts.name: Commit / Retire Logic
parts.role: Retires completed instructions from the ROB head in program order, freeing physical registers and releasing stores to drain to cache.

parts.name: Integer ALU 0
parts.role: Executes one integer arithmetic/logic micro-op per cycle.

parts.name: Integer ALU 1
parts.role: Second integer ALU giving the core dual-issue arithmetic throughput.

parts.name: Branch Resolution Unit
parts.role: Resolves branch outcomes and signals mispredict redirects back to the front end.

parts.name: Integer Multiply / Divide Unit
parts.role: Performs multi-cycle integer multiply and divide operations.

parts.name: FP Fused-Multiply-Add Pipeline
parts.role: Pipelined floating-point multiply-add datapath for the bulk of FP work.

parts.name: FP Divide / Square-Root Unit
parts.role: Iterative unit handling floating-point divide and square-root operations.

parts.name: Operand Bypass / Forwarding Network
parts.role: Forwards each execution unit's result directly to dependent operands a cycle before writeback, so back-to-back dependent micro-ops issue without stalling.

parts.name: Load-Store Unit
parts.role: Generates and disambiguates memory addresses and arbitrates the data-cache port.

parts.name: Data TLB
parts.role: Translates load and store virtual addresses to physical addresses for the data cache; a miss invokes the page table walker.

parts.name: Load Queue
parts.role: Tracks in-flight loads and checks for memory-ordering violations against stores.

parts.name: Store Queue
parts.role: Buffers store addresses and data, forwarding to loads and draining to cache at commit.

parts.name: L1 Data Cache
parts.role: Non-blocking first-level data cache serving loads and accepting committed stores.

parts.name: D-Cache Miss-Status Holding Registers
parts.role: Tracks multiple outstanding data-cache misses so loads and stores keep issuing while refills are in flight.

parts.name: Page Table Walker (PTW)
parts.role: Walks in-memory page tables to refill the instruction and data TLBs on a translation miss.

parts.name: Main Pipeline Data Bus
parts.role: Copper trace carrying the in-order instruction stream from fetch through dispatch.

parts.name: Branch Redirect Bus
parts.role: Copper control trace routing mispredict redirects from the branch unit back to the front-end predictor, GHR, snapshot and FTQ.

parts.name: Writeback Result Bus
parts.role: Copper trace broadcasting committed execution results back to the register files for architectural state.

parts.name: Memory Access Bus
parts.role: Copper trace linking the memory issue queue, load queue, MSHRs and page table walker to the L1 caches.
